Almost every technology boom creates a bubble, then a bust, whether it’s railroads, the Industrial Revolution, or the late 1920s.

Think about the late ‘20s: electricity, refrigeration, telephones, radios, airplanes, and cars were all emerging at once. Naturally, people wanted to invest in these miracles.

The danger is that people fail to distinguish the miracle from the investment. A technology can be truly transformative, but if the stocks are priced too high or bought on debt, you get a crash. That is the mechanics behind how bubbles form and burst.

New technology will be great, there is no doubt about that, but we always have to ask: great for whom, does it pay, and are we paying too much for the miracle?

Sugar in India sits at the intersection of food inflation, farmer incomes, mill economics, ethanol policy, cooperative finance and political power. The government-set minimum selling price for sugar has remained ₹31/kg since February 2019, even as the Fair and Remunerative Price for sugarcane has kept rising and is now ₹365/quintal for 2026–27. As of April, nearly ₹13,000 crore of cane dues for the current season were still unpaid. 

In Maharashtra, this gets even more complicated. Peer-reviewed economic research has found that politically controlled sugar mills can behave differently around elections, including paying farmers lower cane prices in election years. Before Maharashtra’s 2024 election, at least 61 candidates reportedly had links to sugar mills; 35 won. 

And underneath all of those policy debates is the labour actually harvesting the cane. A Maharashtra government inquiry found that 13,861 of 82,309 surveyed women sugarcane cutters in Beed — nearly 17% — had undergone hysterectomies. Separate research in parts of Beed found rates as high as 36%, versus roughly 3% nationally, amid documented pressure created by punishing work conditions, lost wages, debt and lack of menstrual sanitation. 

So no, the explanation is not simply “ethanol took all our sugar.” Ethanol matters. Weather matters. Forecasting errors matter. Prices and policy matter. Politics matters. Labour conditions matter.

Six headlines that look unrelated are actually different layers of the same commodity.

How to do Lat Pulldown 

🎯 Target Muscles: Latissimus Dorsi (Lats), Biceps Brachii

▶ STARTING POSITION

1. Sit facing the weight stack and secure your thighs firmly under the pads.
2. Grip the bar with a closed, pronated grip (palms facing forward), slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Keep your feet firmly on the floor, torso slightly leaned back, and spine neutral.
4. Extend your arms fully and maintain a stable position throughout the movement.

▶ DOWNWARD MOVEMENT

5. Pull the bar down toward the upper chest while driving the elbows down and slightly backward.
6. Keep the chest lifted and torso stable. Avoid swinging or leaning backward excessively.
7. Bring the bar toward the upper chest/clavicle area in a controlled manner.

▶ UPWARD MOVEMENT

8. Slowly return the bar to the starting position under control.
9. Allow the elbows to fully extend without letting the weight pull your arms up suddenly.
10. Maintain the same torso position throughout the movement.

Priya: I have lived in the US for eight years. But I cannot vote, and my stay here is never
truly guaranteed.

Meghna: I also lived here for eight years. But I can vote, and my stay is 100% permanent.

Same country. Same timeline. But one of them is still one mistake away from losing
everything.

Priya is a Green Card holder, while Meghna naturalized as a US citizen.

As a Green Card holder, you can’t vote in any US election. As a citizen, you get full voting
rights.

A Green Card can still be revoked, and minor legal offenses might risk your stay in the US.

But as a citizen, your protection is permanent you can never be deported.

And here’s where the real power lies: Green Card holders cannot sponsor their parents for a visa. Citizens can, with zero annual caps and no waiting line.

Stay outside the US for over six months, and your Green Card risks abandonment.

But here’s a catch: becoming a US citizen means permanently surrendering your Indian
passport. 
#India doesn’t allow dual citizenship, so you get an OCI card instead.

A Green Card gives you stability. Citizenship gives you security, but costs your Indian

Sauna post-resistance training may enhance muscle growth.

I just finished resistance training, and now I’m in the sauna. What interests me is whether heat can do more than help recovery but whether it can influence how our muscles adapt to training.

A new meta-analysis from Dr. Brad Schoenfeld (@bradschoenfeldphd) and colleagues combined six studies involving 125 people. It found a small, possible advantage for muscle growth when heat was applied after lifting but no clear additional strength benefit. The studies had limitations, so this is encouraging, not conclusive. 

Heat is itself a cellular stressor. Human muscle-biopsy research has shown that adding whole-body heat after resistance exercise can increase heat-shock protein expression and activate mTOR signaling, part of the machinery that regulates muscle protein synthesis. That provides a plausible mechanism. 

My protocol is about 20 minutes in a hot sauna at 180 F after lifting, because I’m interested not just in potential muscle adaptations, but in long-term cardiovascular and brain health. In Finnish men followed for about 20 years, sauna use 4-7 times per week was associated with 40% lower all-cause mortality, 50% lower cardiovascular mortality, and 66% lower dementia risk.

He Paid ₹41 Lakh for a ₹13 Lakh Land Purchase

A US-based NRI got hit with a penalty of around ₹41 lakh. Not for a scam. Not for hiding money. But for buying a property in India.

NRIs can buy properties of any form, except agricultural land, plantation property, or farmhouses. FEMA draws a hard line around these.

An NRI cannot buy them. They can’t even receive it as a gift, even from parents. The only legal way to own it is inheritance.

This is exactly where that US citizen got it wrong. He bought agricultural property in Tamil Nadu for ₹13.68 lakh, without getting the prior RBI approval the law requires.

The original penalty calculated came close to ₹1.5 crore a base amount plus a share of the gain he made. FEMA caps penalties at three times the contravention amount, so it was brought down. 
He still ended up paying around ₹41 lakh, on a ₹13.68 lakh purchase.

If you’re buying land anywhere near a farm, plantation, or countryside plot, stop and check before you sign anything.

Are you sure that “countryside plot” you’re eyeing isn’t classified as agricultural land?

My guest on the podcast is Joe Liemandt, the principal of Alpha school, where kids spend two hours a day learning cognitive skills and the rest of the time learning practical skills. Their performance on standardized tests, but also in life are astounding, so clearly they’re onto something.

I have no relationship to Alpha school financially or otherwise but I’m intrigued by what can allow learning to be more effective at all ages. The episode shares a lot of useful information that anyone can apply to learning anything. For kids and for adult adults.

Why don’t we always train to failure?

Research shows that a large portion of the hypertrophy and strength benefits can be achieved when a set is stopped within a few reps of failure, without the higher recovery cost and form breakdown associated with true failure.

A range of 1–3 RIR can provide an effective stimulus while helping maintain training quality throughout the session.

RIR can also help correct two common mistakes:

Some people think every set should be taken to failure, while others always stop at 5+ RIR.

RIR = Reps in Reserve

It refers to the number of quality reps you could still perform when a set ends.

For example, 2 RIR means that after finishing the set, you could still perform 2 clean reps.

RIR has a direct relationship with RPE:

RPE 8 ≈ 2 RIR
RPE 9 ≈ 1 RIR
RPE 10 = 0 RIR / Failure

They’re essentially two ways of describing the same concept. RIR is often easier for athletes to understand because instead of asking them to rate intensity abstractly, it asks:

“How many more reps could you have done?”

RIR in the OPT Model

Stabilization & Endurance: ~3–5 RIR
Hypertrophy: mostly 1–3 RIR
Strength: 1–3 RIR on heavy sets
0 RIR: only in rare, planned, and supervised situations

RIR can also be used for weekly progression:

Week 1 → 3 RIR
Week 2 → 2 RIR
Week 3 → 1 RIR
Then → Deload

Combined with the 2-for-2 rule for increasing weight, RIR can create a complete autoregulated progression system.

📚 Source: National Academy of Sports Medicine (NASM)

Taking Cash for Your Property Sale? Watch this first

I almost made a huge mistake while selling my Bangalore flat last year.

The buyer seemed serious, and said he wanted to pay 30 lakhs in cash. Honestly, for a moment, I considered it too. Registering the property at a lower value, and taking the rest in cash, can save on capital gains tax.

But as an NRI, I can’t just sit on 30 lakhs in cash in India.
If I deposit it in my bank account, income tax wants to know where it came from. 

If I give it to a family member to deposit, now they’re in trouble too. And taking it abroad is a completely
different legal problem.

Here’s what made me walk away completely.

If the income tax department pulls this transaction for scrutiny and property deals above a certain value almost always get flagged  both me and the buyer pay tax on the same 30 lakhs. 

He pays tax on it as unexplained income, at a rate far higher than any tax he’d have saved. I pay capital gains on the full actual sale value.

We both lose more than we saved.

I went back to the buyer and said: just to save 7% stamp duty, you’re going to pay 12.5% capital gains when you sell this flat later, calculated on an understated cost.

We split the stamp duty difference and did the entire transaction through banking channels.

If you’re an NRI selling property in India right now, has anyone suggested you take part of the payment in cash?

And to understand his argument, let’s unpack the three constraints that define AI in the world right now...

1/ Electricity 

Whenever you ask any question to a ChatGPT, Claude or any other model... the query is answered by semiconductor chips at a data centre that run a lot of computational data to give you the answer... and this requires a lot of power...

Such that, right now the US is facing a structural problem with electricity...

Where China currently generates more electricity than the US, Europe, and India combined... and in the past one year itself, it has added 40% of the entire US grid’s capacity of power... and created the whole US power grid’s capacity in just 4 years...

So it is soon on a path to produce almost 4 times the electricity that the US produces in a year... that too with renewables, which are cheaper...

Whereas in the US, the proposed new power plants are stuck such that they may take anywhere between 5-12 years to connect to the grid...

So the US is about to lose very rapidly to China when it comes to the first constraint or raw material - electricity.

2/ Chips

Right now, Nvidia makes the best chips in the world, but the US has put constraints on Nvidia shipping chips to China - where higher tariff would be imposed on chips being pushed to China because they are trying to starve China of access to chips...

But quite like ASML makes the machines for creating chips, China has set up a company called SMIC which is already making chips 7 nm small... getting to 5 nm, and would soon reach a point where they can create their equally capable chips as well...

3/ AI Models

China’s DeepSeek V4 Flash and Kimi K3 are already very good, and while being ranked in the top 5 models in the world, are already producing US model level output at 10% the cost...
